source_policy.note: Health-related values require source provenance. Missing values remain null rather than guessed.
source_policy.official_first_note: K-FIND currently exposes integrated nutrition data and Open API; catalog entries may exist before nutrient values are mapped, but production UI must not invent missing values.

rules: Never replace missing nutrition with zero.
Keep source URL, authority, dataset/item identifier, retrieval date and verification status.
Allergen rules are jurisdiction-aware; U.S. major-9 is one baseline, not a universal worldwide list.
Fish, crustacean shellfish and tree nuts retain species/type where available.

K_FIND.authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (Korea)

progress.note: 1,000-item catalog capacity milestone reached. Placeholder rows are explicitly marked pending curation and must not be shown as verified foods; next phase replaces them with curated names and official nutrient mappings.
progress.next_priority: Continue alias QA and classify exact-name duplicate candidates before official K-FIND nutrient matching.

ingestion_plan.strategy: official bulk/API first, manual verification for ambiguous foods

ingestion_plan.next_step: Populate nutrition_records from official K-FIND first for Korean/common foods, then USDA FoodData Central for global coverage; preserve preparation-specific records.

nutrition_record_schema.description: Source-mapped nutrient records. Never overwrite one preparation/country record with another.

production_rules: Never expose placeholder_pending_curation rows in search or suggestions.
Do not invent nutrient values when an official source match is absent.
Keep preparation-specific foods as separate nutrient records.
Resolve duplicate names by canonical ingredient id and aliases before nutrient mapping.

USDA FoodData Central for global gaps
